299:/// NOTE: All information in cs_detail is only available when CS_OPT_DETAIL = CS_OPT_ON
300:/// Initialized as memset(., 0, offsetof(cs_detail, ARCH)+sizeof(cs_ARCH))
301-/// by ARCH_getInstruction in arch/ARCH/ARCHDisassembler.c
302:/// if cs_detail changes, in particular if a field is added after the union,
303-/// then update arch/ARCH/ARCHDisassembler.c accordingly
304:typedef struct cs_detail {
305-    uint16_t regs_read[16]; ///< list of implicit registers read by this insn
306-    uint8_t regs_read_count; ///< number of implicit registers read by this insn
307-
308-    uint16_t regs_write[20]; ///< list of implicit registers modified by this insn

314-    /// Architecture-specific instruction info
315-    union {
316-            cs_x86 x86;     ///< X86 architecture, including 16-bit, 32-bit & 64-bit mode
317-            cs_arm64 arm64; ///< ARM64 architecture (aka AArch64)
318-            cs_arm arm;     ///< ARM architecture (including Thumb/Thumb2)
319-            cs_m68k m68k;   ///< M68K architecture
320-            cs_mips mips;   ///< MIPS architecture
321-            cs_ppc ppc;         ///< PowerPC architecture

323-            cs_sysz sysz;   ///< SystemZ architecture
324-            cs_xcore xcore; ///< XCore architecture
325-            cs_tms320c64x tms320c64x;  ///< TMS320C64x architecture
326-            cs_m680x m680x; ///< M680X architecture
327-            cs_evm evm;         ///< Ethereum architecture
328-            cs_mos65xx mos65xx;     ///< MOS65XX architecture (including MOS6502)
329-            cs_wasm wasm;   ///< Web Assembly architecture
330-            cs_bpf bpf;     ///< Berkeley Packet Filter architecture (including eBPF)
331-            cs_riscv riscv; ///< RISCV architecture
332-    };
333:} cs_detail;

335-/// Detail information of disassembled instruction
336-typedef struct cs_insn {
337-    /// Instruction ID (basically a numeric ID for the instruction mnemonic)
338-    /// Find the instruction id in the '[ARCH]_insn' enum in the header file
339-    /// of corresponding architecture, such as 'arm_insn' in arm.h for ARM,
340-    /// 'x86_insn' in x86.h for X86, etc...
341-    /// This information is available even when CS_OPT_DETAIL = CS_OPT_OFF
342-    /// NOTE: in Skipdata mode, "data" instruction has 0 for this id field.
343-    unsigned int id;
344-
345-    /// Address (EIP) of this instruction
346-    /// This information is available even when CS_OPT_DETAIL = CS_OPT_OFF
347-    uint64_t address;
348-
349-    /// Size of this instruction
350-    /// This information is available even when CS_OPT_DETAIL = CS_OPT_OFF
351-    uint16_t size;
352-
353-    /// Machine bytes of this instruction, with number of bytes indicated by @size above
354-    /// This information is available even when CS_OPT_DETAIL = CS_OPT_OFF
355-    uint8_t bytes[24];
356-
357-    /// Ascii text of instruction mnemonic
358-    /// This information is available even when CS_OPT_DETAIL = CS_OPT_OFF
359-    char mnemonic[CS_MNEMONIC_SIZE];
360-
361-    /// Ascii text of instruction operands
362-    /// This information is available even when CS_OPT_DETAIL = CS_OPT_OFF
363-    char op_str[160];
364-
365:    /// Pointer to cs_detail.
366-    /// NOTE: detail pointer is only valid when both requirements below are met:
367-    /// (1) CS_OP_DETAIL = CS_OPT_ON
368-    /// (2) Engine is not in Skipdata mode (CS_OP_SKIPDATA option set to CS_OPT_ON)
369-    ///
370-    /// NOTE 2: when in Skipdata mode, or when detail mode is OFF, even if this pointer
371-    ///     is not NULL, its content is still irrelevant.
372:    cs_detail *detail;
373-} cs_insn;
374-
375-
376-/// Calculate the offset of a disassembled instruction in its buffer, given its position
377-/// in its array of disassembled insn
378-/// NOTE: this macro works with position (>=1), not index
379-#define CS_INSN_OFFSET(insns, post) (insns[post - 1].address - insns[0].address)

383-/// These are values returned by cs_errno()
384-typedef enum cs_err {
385-    CS_ERR_OK = 0,   ///< No error: everything was fine
386-    CS_ERR_MEM,      ///< Out-Of-Memory error: cs_open(), cs_disasm(), cs_disasm_iter()
387-    CS_ERR_ARCH,     ///< Unsupported architecture: cs_open()
388-    CS_ERR_HANDLE,   ///< Invalid handle: cs_op_count(), cs_op_index()
389-    CS_ERR_CSH,      ///< Invalid csh argument: cs_close(), cs_errno(), cs_option()
390-    CS_ERR_MODE,     ///< Invalid/unsupported mode: cs_open()
391-    CS_ERR_OPTION,   ///< Invalid/unsupported option: cs_option()
392-    CS_ERR_DETAIL,   ///< Information is unavailable because detail option is OFF
393-    CS_ERR_MEMSETUP, ///< Dynamic memory management uninitialized (see CS_OPT_MEM)
394-    CS_ERR_VERSION,  ///< Unsupported version (bindings)
395-    CS_ERR_DIET,     ///< Access irrelevant data in "diet" engine
396-    CS_ERR_SKIPDATA, ///< Access irrelevant data for "data" instruction in SKIPDATA mode
397-    CS_ERR_X86_ATT,  ///< X86 AT&T syntax is unsupported (opt-out at compile time)
398-    CS_ERR_X86_INTEL, ///< X86 Intel syntax is unsupported (opt-out at compile time)
